scope: Primary-source research; pool support is not an exhaustive census of every Scrypt auxiliary chain.
publishableHeading: One Scrypt engine. Several independent chains.
explanation: Compatible auxiliary chains can reuse a miner's Scrypt proof of work. The chains keep separate rules, balances and blocks; shared work does not merge their ledgers or make security identical.

poolPayoutDistinctions.note: Eligible LTC PPS+ or PPLNS miners receive auxiliary rewards under PPLNS. Amounts vary. Current official guide dated September 15, 2026.
Current FAQ dated June 29, 2026 requires activated payout addresses. Unconfigured rewards are waived; thresholds apply.
Direct payouts are LTC and DOGE. Other profitable auxiliary coins contribute to its PPS rate; its FAQ does not provide a definitive current auxiliary-chain roster.
Official pool page says merge-mined coins are converted to LTC. A payout asset is not proof that the corresponding chain was mined.

economics.publishable: DOGE and other auxiliary rewards can diversify mining revenue. A miner may choose to sell those rewards toward electricity costs and retain LTC, but whether that covers the bill depends on output, prices, pool rules and operating costs.
economics.formula: Operating margin = LTC revenue + auxiliary-coin revenue + fees earned - electricity - pool fees - hosting and maintenance.
economics.illustrativeEnergyFormula: Daily electricity cost = device kilowatts × 24 × electricity price per kWh; label any example assumptions.
avoid: DOGE always pays the energy bill
miners never need to sell LTC
same Scrypt algorithm alone makes a coin merge-mineable
all auxiliary tokens are directly paid to every miner

digitalSilver.publishable: Digital silver is Litecoin's long-running analogy: a limited issuance schedule and faster target blocks alongside Bitcoin's digital-gold narrative. It is a community description, not metal backing, a fixed BTC/LTC price ratio or a promise of investment returns.
